text:
nina.sales: CorpX wants a concise network + cost answer for their Private Deploy POC. They asked: 1) recommended topology (peering vs PrivateLink), 2) exact firewall rules to paste into their questionnaire, 3) who pays what if traffic goes through their egress proxy vs interface endpoint, and 4) any operational gotchas (SNAT, TLS-inspect). Need a single message I can paste back.

arthur.net: Recommend PrivateLink (interface endpoints) for POCs that require least-privilege isolation. Peering is fine for intra-account low-latency needs but it exposes routes and is harder to scope for security reviews.

pat.platform: Pasteable firewall snippet (PrivateLink):
```
Outbound from app subnets -> interface endpoint private IPs (we'll supply list):
- Protocol: TCP
- Port: 443
- Destination: <InterfaceEndpointPrivateIPs> (3-5 IPs per region typical)
Optional: UDP 123 -> internal NTP if you enforce host time sync
Notes: allow TLS passthrough for these IPs if you use TLS-inspecting proxies to preserve mTLS and certificate pinning.
```

gina.sec: Add validation and attestation lines for questionnaire:
- Validate server cert chain and SAN for our service hostnames; we'll provide cert thumbprint(s) during onboarding.
- For Private Deploy connector: mTLS available; we'll exchange client certs and CA details.
- KMS/BYOK: we support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest; include request to attach KMS ARN during onboarding.

nina.sales: Clear. What about cost sentence we can paste into the RFP re: egress vs endpoint charges?

pat.platform: One-liner for RFP: "Recommended: use AWS PrivateLink for isolated POC traffic; AWS interface endpoint hourly and per-GB charges are billed to the customeraccount. Public NAT/egress through a corporate proxy will be charged as normal cloud egress by the cloud provider. Redwood can provide egress-inclusive estimates for Dedicated/Private quotes on request."

arthur.net: Who pays which charges: if you create Interface Endpoints in your account you pay the endpoint hourly and per-GB data processing fees. If you route traffic via your NAT/proxy to our public IPs, your cloud bill records standard egress; Redwood does not offset cloud provider egress fees unless negotiated in the Dedicated/Private contract.

gina.sec: Important security caveat to paste: TLS-inspecting proxies will break mTLS and may break our client cert validation. If you must inspect TLS, please whitelist our endpoint IPs for passthrough or configure the proxy to preserve SNI and allow certificate pinning. We publish cert thumbprints and expect customers to verify them during onboarding.

arthur.net: Operational SNAT note: NAT gateway ephemeral ports are finite (~64k per IP, fewer usable). For high-concurrency load tests (many short-lived TCP connections), recommend connection reuse (HTTP/2 or keepalive), multiple NAT IPs, or multiple NAT gateways. We can supply concurrency vs ephemeral port guidance once you share expected RPS.

nina.sales: Can someone give a final combined reply I can paste to CorpX security team (brief)?

pat.platform: Paste-ready response: 
"We recommend using AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) for an isolated POC. This avoids cross-account peering and makes allowlisting straightforward. Please add outbound TCP/443 to the interface endpoint private IPs (we will supply 305 IPs per region) and optionally UDP/123 for NTP. If you route traffic via a corporate egress proxy or NAT, note that your cloud bill will reflect standard egress charges; interface endpoint hourly/per-GB costs are billed to the customeraccount. Also note TLS-inspection can break mTLS/cert pinning; we recommend TLS passthrough to our endpoint IPs or preserving SNI and cert chains. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private Deploys and will provide SOC2/ISO docs and cert thumbprints during onboarding. For load testing, coordinate expected RPS so we can advise on NAT ephemeral port mitigation"

infra-bot: INF-8230 created to provision PrivateLink ENIs and return IP list; will post to this thread when ready.

nina.sales: Perfect, thanks all. I'll send this to CorpX along with a request for a network contact to produce an ATO-style diagram. (emoji :white_check_mark:)
